response.sql:
WITH patient_labs AS (
  SELECT 
    p.ID,
    p.SEX,
    l.PT,
    CASE WHEN l.IGA IS NOT NULL AND l.IGM IS NOT NULL THEN l.IGA - l.IGM ELSE NULL END AS iga_igm_diff
  FROM Laboratory l
  INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID
),
patient_aggregates AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    SEX,
    AVG(PT) as avg_pt,
    AVG(iga_igm_diff) as avg_iga_igm_diff
  FROM patient_labs
  GROUP BY ID, SEX
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_iga_igm_diff) as overall_mean_iga_igm
  FROM patient_aggregates
),
patient_with_ratio AS (
  SELECT 
    pa.ID,
    pa.SEX,
    pa.avg_pt,
    pa.avg_iga_igm_diff,
    pa.avg_iga_igm_diff / NULLIF(om.overall_mean_iga_igm, 0) as ratio_to_overall_mean
  FROM patient_aggregates pa
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
)
SELECT 
  SEX,
  AVG(avg_pt) as avg_pt,
  AVG(avg_iga_igm_diff) as avg_iga_igm_diff,
  AVG(ratio_to_overall_mean) as avg_ratio_to_overall_mean
FROM patient_with_ratio
GROUP BY SEX
ORDER BY SEX;

assumptions.assumption: "the mean across all patients" refers to the mean of each patient's IGA-IGM average (patient-level aggregation), not the global mean across all lab records
When both IGA and IGM are null for a lab record, that record is excluded from the patient's IGA-IGM average; only records with both values present contribute

alternatives.interpretation: "The mean across all patients" means the global mean of all (IGA-IGM) differences computed from individual lab records, rather than the mean of patient-level averages
